summary: The attempt-3 atomicity fix is correct and independently verified: Plugin.UpdateConfiguration validates the candidate before base.UpdateConfiguration persists anything, the validate/persist/activate sequence is serialized by a per-plugin lock, the old TryRestoreLastValidConfiguration path is gone, and the new concurrent-save regression test is genuine (it fails under a reconstructed pre-fix implementation). Targeted tests (20) and the full suite (1260 passed / 63 skipped / 1323 total) reproduce the worker's numbers, build is 0 warnings / 0 errors, and the SEC-9.3-02/03/04 hardening items are present and tested. However, the rework left stale 'restored' wording that contradicts the implemented validate-before-persist flow in ADR-021 clause 4, the PLANS.md Project Status paragraph, and docs/limitations.md F2, plus 'call base and then TryReplace' wording in the PLANS.md 9.3 objective/work bullets. The worker's claim that these overclaims were corrected across those surfaces is inaccurate, so the task's documentation-accuracy requirement is not yet met.

findings.summary: Residual 'restored' wording contradicts the implemented validate-before-persist flow.
findings.detail: Three canonical/decision surfaces still describe a restore step that no longer exists, contradicting ADR-016 clause 4 and ADR-021 clause 5 and the code (an invalid candidate is never passed to base.UpdateConfiguration, so nothing is restored). (1) docs/decisions.md:2624-2627 (ADR-021 clause 4): 'a notifier failure does not affect the rejection, the retained snapshot/secrets, or the restored persisted configuration' - there is no restored persisted configuration; clause 5 of the same ADR says the rejected candidate is never persisted. (2) PLANS.md:19 (Project Status paragraph): task 9.3 '... retains the last valid public snapshot and private secret generation and restores the last valid persisted configuration on an invalid candidate ...'. (3) docs/limitations.md:97-102 (F2 Current state): 'Task 9.3 overrides Plugin.UpdateConfiguration to call the host base implementation and then validate and activate the candidate at runtime ... and the last valid configuration is restored so a rejected save does not leave an invalid candidate in ArrTags.xml.' All three contradict src/ArrTags/Plugin.cs:138-153, where validation precedes persistence and base is only called for a valid candidate.
findings.recommended_action: Reword these three lines to the implemented guarantee: the candidate is validated before base persists anything, an invalid candidate is never written, and the last valid configuration remains active and persisted (no restore step). Keep ADR-021 clause 4 consistent with clause 5.

findings.summary: PLANS.md 9.3 objective/work bullets still describe the old 'base then TryReplace' ordering.
findings.detail: PLANS.md:3645-3648 (9.3 Objective) says 'Override Plugin.UpdateConfiguration to call base and then ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace' and PLANS.md:3665-3667 (Work) says 'Override UpdateConfiguration: call base.UpdateConfiguration(configuration), then ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace(...)'. The implemented (and separately documented in the same section's Status) ordering is validate -> if valid, base -> TryReplace; an invalid candidate never reaches base. This is the exact residual 'base then TryReplace' wording the task asked to eliminate. It is lower severity than DOC-9.3-A3-01 because the section's Status paragraph is already correct, but it is inconsistent with it.
findings.recommended_action: Update the 9.3 Objective/Work bullets to the validate-before-persist ordering (validate; for a valid candidate, base then TryReplace), matching the Status paragraph.

rework_log: Attempt 2 was approved by the implementation reviewer but the independent security review reproduced MEDIUM SEC-9.3-01 (non-atomic Plugin.UpdateConfiguration: concurrent saves could diverge the running snapshot, Plugin.Configuration, and persisted XML; a crash could persist a rejected candidate). Attempt 3 addressed it by validating before base.UpdateConfiguration and serializing the validate/persist/activate sequence, and removed TryRestoreLastValidConfiguration.
Attempt 3 re-review (this report): the functional fix and hardening are verified correct; only documentation residuals remain, so this attempt requires a documentation-only correction.
verified_claims: Atomicity: src/ArrTags/Plugin.cs:138-153 validates with PluginConfigurationValidator.Validate(candidate) before any persistence; base.UpdateConfiguration is called only inside if (result.IsValid); the whole validate/persist/activate sequence is inside lock (_configurationSaveGate). Verified by inspection and by the reconstructed-pre-fix falsification test.
No restore path: TryRestoreLastValidConfiguration/lastValid are absent from src (grep found no matches).
No duplicated validation logic: Plugin calls the existing PluginConfigurationValidator; ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace also uses it (defense in depth, same logic).
Valid saves unchanged: ValidSaveActivatesTheNewSnapshotWithoutRestart passes; the snapshot version increments and both Plugin.Configuration and the persisted XML match the candidate.

Never-throw: UpdateConfigurationNeverThrows, InvalidSaveDoesNotThrowWhenTheNotifierFailsAndRetainsLastValid, UpdateConfigurationDoesNotThrowWhenTheSnapshotServiceIsUnavailable pass; plugin-added paths catch Exception when not OutOfMemoryException. base.UpdateConfiguration is intentionally not wrapped (preserves host behaviour; documented).

notes: The functional rework is sound; the only open items are documentation corrections (DOC-9.3-A3-01/02). No implementation change is required.

The lock is the necessary fix for the two-valid-saves divergence case (without it, base persist and TryReplace could interleave and leave snapshot != persisted); the validate-before-persist change is the necessary fix for the invalid-candidate/restore race. Both are present.
No new security review was produced for attempt 3; that is the orchestrator's separate gate and is not treated as a finding here.
Temporary artifacts under /tmp/9.3/ (oldimpl reconstruction and oldblock.txt) are reviewer-owned; the directory may be removed.
